title: The Man Is Ever Blest
description: The Man Is Ever Blest in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 1, part 2, headed “The saint happy, the sinner miserable”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The man is ev-er blest Who shuns the sin-ner's ways, A-mong their coun-sels nev-er stands, Nor takes the scor-ner's place;

lines: But makes the Law of God
Amidst the labours of the day,
He like a tree shall thrive,
Fresh as the leaf his name shall live,
Their hopes shall flee like empty chaff
How will they bear to stand
Where all the saints at Christ's right hand
But sinners and their works shall meet

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
